specAnchors.text: understand how the structure of the male and female reproductive systems are adapted for their functions

primer.text: Two systems, one goal. This note walks the male and female reproductive tracts part by part — ducts, glands, tubes and rings of muscle — and shows how each structure's build suits its job, from the scrotum's cooling of sperm to the cilia that usher an egg toward the only place fertilisation can happen.

modules.title: The Male Reproductive System
modules.opening: The male system is a production-and-delivery line: testes outside the body make sperm and testosterone, the sperm duct carries them to be mixed with gland fluids, and the urethra inside the penis releases the semen while a ring of muscle keeps urine out of the mixture.
keyPoints: Sperm travel up the sperm duct and pick up gland fluids before ejaculation.
The urethra runs down the penis and carries urine or semen, never both at once.
The testes produce sperm and the hormone testosterone.
The scrotum holds the testes outside the body, keeping them a touch cooler than core body heat.
The penis is the delivery organ: it passes urine out and deposits semen in the vagina at intercourse.

low.restatement: Testes make the cells, the duct delivers them, glands add fluid, and the urethra is the shared exit with a muscle gate.
low.analogy: A factory with an outside cold room (the scrotum), a conveyor (the duct) and a dual-use loading gate (the urethra).
low.examPointer: The dual role of the urethra and the cooler position of the testes are the classic exam facts here.

medium.restatement: Sperm production runs best below core temperature, which is why the scrotum hangs the testes clear of the warm body wall; the gland secretions added in the sperm duct form semen, and the urethral muscle ring prevents urine contaminating the ejaculate.
medium.analogy: A brewery kept in a cellar so the product matures right, with a clean one-way tap.
medium.examPointer: Say slightly lower than body temperature when you explain the scrotum — precision scores.

modules.title: The Female Reproductive System
modules.opening: The female system pairs a gamete nursery with a nursery for the fetus itself: ovaries release mature ova, ciliated oviducts carry them and host fertilisation, the muscular uterus hosts the implanting embryo, and cervix plus vagina guard and admit at the right moments.
keyPoints: Ovaries hold the ova, which ripen and develop as hormones are released.
Oviducts join each ovary to the uterus; their ciliated lining nudges the released ovum along.
The uterus is a muscular organ whose soft lining receives the implanting embryo and supports its growth.
The cervix is a ring of muscle keeping the fetus in place; the vagina receives sperm during intercourse.

low.restatement: Ovaries store and release eggs, oviducts ferry them and host fertilisation, the uterus grows the fetus, and the cervix seals it in.
low.analogy: A hatchery (ovary), a conveyor belt (oviduct), a maternity ward (uterus) and a locked door (cervix).
low.examPointer: Attach cilia to the oviduct and muscle to the cervix — structural detail carries the adaptation marks.

medium.restatement: Every wall is purpose-built: cilia sweep the ovum toward the uterus, the uterus's muscle and soft lining accept and nourish an implanted embryo, and the cervical ring holds the growing fetus sealed until birth.
medium.analogy: An airport with moving walkways, a hotel suite and a security door, each serving one passenger stage.
medium.examPointer: Name where fertilisation occurs — inside the oviduct — when asked for adaptations.

glossary.definition: The tube through the penis that carries urine or semen out of the body.
The sac of skin supporting the testes outside the body at a lower temperature.
The ciliated tube linking ovary and uterus where fertilisation occurs.
The ring of muscle at the lower end of the uterus that keeps the fetus in place.
